items.title: African leaders herald $16B Dangote oil refinery in Kenya
items.summary: An oil refinery on Kenya's coast is expected to be completed in 40 months, and will process an estimated 700,000 barrels of oil per day. Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, will lead the project African leaders on Wednesday broke ground on a new $16 billion (€14 billion) oil refinery off Kenya's coast The project is expected to be completed in 40 months, and will process an estimated 700,000 barrels of oil per day. The refinery will be constructed at the coastal town of Lamu Kenya's President William Ruto, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed were among the leaders who attended an event to celebrate the project, the largest of its kind in East and Central Africa The refinery "will strengthen regional energy security, reduce reliance on imports and bolster our foreign exchange," Ruto said on social media "But this is more than a refinery.

items.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
items.summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU. An African partner country has reportedly already been selected Deportation centers are legally contentious, expensive and the subject of political controversy: For years, Brussels has been grappling with the issue of establishing such centers outside the EU for rejected asylum seekers. Previous attempts have failed due to legal objections, but now, a "group of five" consisting of Greece , Germany , Austria , Denmark and the Netherlands believes it has overcome these hurdles During an interview with the Greek television channel ANT1, Greece's Minister of Migration, Thanos Plevris, stated that the first of these so-called " return hubs " is scheduled to begin operations as early as the second half of 2027 — just in time for Greece to assume the EU Council Presidency Plevris said Greece had chosen an African country but could not reveal its name yet.

items.title: Dams above 90% capacity raise concern in northern Mozambique
items.summary: Mozambique is preparing to experience opposite impacts of the same weather phenomenon, El Niño, during the rainy season that officially begins on 1 October. While the South is expected to face a shortage of rainfall, the North could receive abundant rainfall “During this period of October, November and December we are talking about 50 to 80 millimetres, but in the first quarter of 2027 we are expecting cyclones, so we expect rainfall of 120 to 200 millimetres per day, and this is rainfall that has brought extremely high impacts. We are talking about the months of January, February and March,” warned Carlitos Omar, director-general of the Northern Regional Water Administration, ARA-Norte The situation is even more concerning because the six dams under the jurisdiction of the Northern Regional Water Administration are currently at more than 90% capacity.

items.title: Disbursement of almost 50 million meticais for acquisition of vehicles sparks public criticism
items.summary: Maputo, 30 Sep – Disbursement of 49.5 million meticais (175, 000 US dollars at the current exchange rate) for acquisition of vehicles for the Constitutional Council (CC) – Mozambique’s highest body on constitutional and electoral law – sparks public criticism following the selection of four suppliers. The controversy follows a publication in the daily newspaper “Notícias”, in which the CC awarded four contracts for the acquisition of vehicles with values ranging from 1.9 million to 27. 8 million meticais (from 29,000 to 435,000 US dollars at the current exchange rate). The publication points out that a contract worth 27.8 million meticais for a Mercedes-Benz vehicle was awarded to Multi Franchise Comércio Automóvel, while an 18 million meticais contract for a Hyundai Palisade was awarded to Ronil, Limitada. The document also points out that a 1.9 million meticais contract for a Toyota Hiace and 1.7 million meticais for a Toyota a Hilux 4×4 was awarded to Brumarine Rent A Car SU, Limitada.

items.title: Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
items.summary: Aliko Dangote made his fortune in cement before branching into oil Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and Kenya's President William Ruto have broken ground on a $16bn (£12bn) oil refinery in Lamu, on Kenya's northern coast Upon completion, the refinery is expected to process 700,000 barrels of crude oil a day, making it East Africa's largest industrial project by capacity Ahead of the launch, some local residents took to the streets to demand more compensation for land used for the refinery Speaking to the BBC, Dangote, Africa's richest man, dismissed the protests as games played by local marketers and international players, insisting the refinery would go ahead and would be ready by 2030 as planned The ground-breaking was also attended by the leaders of Uganda, Ethiopia, Togo and Benin Dangote has offered regional governments a combined 30% stake in the refinery, according to Reuters news agency "This is Africa coming together to build Africa.

items.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
items.summary: Russia has launched the largest attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the spring, primarily targeting Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukraine's Prime Minister has said At least five people were killed in overnight attacks across the country, including a child in the Kyiv region, Serhiy Koretskyi said The strikes also impacted people's power supplies, with Ukraine's biggest private energy firm DTEK saying power to 8,000 homes had been restored following "a difficult night" for the capital The Russian defence ministry said one of its targets was the Trypilska power station, the largest supplier of electricity to Kyiv. The operator confirmed damage to the plant Koretskyi wrote on Telegram: "Since the summer, there has effectively not been a single day without enemy attacks on our energy infrastructure "However, a mass and combined attack of this scale has occurred for the first time since the end of the last heating season." Ukraine has been expecting another protracted Russian assault on the country's energy grid.

items.title: Are the Houthis winning against Saudi Arabia?
items.summary: It's unclear how the Saudis can defuse the threat presented by the Houthis in next-door Yemen or who they can turn to for help. The US isn't interested, the Europeans are hedging and nobody wants open conflict with Iran Last week, some students in Saudi Arabia were told they should stay at home and attend classes online, due to continued threats from attacks by the Houthi group in neighboring Yemen. But the very next day, they were given the all-clear and allowed to return to school in person The conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia in Yemen seems to have become part of everyday life in Saudi Arabia. After a period of comparative calm , the Houthis have been ramping up attacks on the country, starting July, and have fired many missiles and drones over the border Over recent weeks, the Houthi militia have also pushed further into Yemen , taking more control of the Yemeni coast and several islands in the Red Sea. This means they can oversee maritime traffic in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
